title: Python Iterators, Generators & Context Managers: Revision Notes
summary: Quick revision of Python's iteration protocol, generators and yield, generator expressions, itertools essentials, lazy evaluation and context managers. Built for night-before recall, from mental model to cheat sheet.

chapters.title: Iterables, Iterators and the Protocol
points: Iterable = has __iter__() returning an iterator; iterator = has __next__() and __iter__() returning self
for loop calls iter(obj) once, then next() repeatedly until StopIteration is raised
Lists, tuples, dicts and strs are iterables but not iterators (file objects are their own iterators); iter([1,2]) gives a list_iterator
An iterator is single-pass and stateful: once exhausted, next() keeps raising StopIteration
next(it, default) returns default instead of raising StopIteration at the end

chapters.title: Generators and yield
points: A function containing yield returns a generator object when called; the body does not run until the first next()
yield pauses the function and keeps local state; the next next() resumes right after the yield
Falling off the end or a bare return raises StopIteration; return value becomes StopIteration.value
yield from sub delegates to a sub-iterable and passes its return value back
gen.send(x) makes the paused yield evaluate to x (prime with next() first); gen.close() raises GeneratorExit inside

chapters.title: Generator Expressions and Lazy Evaluation
points: Syntax (x*x for x in data if x>0) with round brackets builds a generator, not a list
List comp [..] builds everything now in O(n) memory; generator expr yields one item at a time in O(1) memory
Drop the extra parentheses when it is the sole argument: sum(x*x for x in data)
Lazy pipelines chain generators so each item flows through every stage before the next is read
A generator can be consumed only once; iterating it a second time yields nothing, and len() and indexing do not work

chapters.title: itertools Essentials
points: count(start, step), cycle(it) and repeat(x, n) make infinite or repeated streams; stop them with islice or break
islice(it, stop) or islice(it, start, stop, step) slices any iterator lazily; negative indices are not allowed
chain(a, b) and chain.from_iterable(list_of_lists) concatenate iterables without copying
groupby(it, key) groups only consecutive equal keys, so sort by the same key first
zip_longest, product, permutations, combinations: product(a, b) is the nested-loop cartesian product; combinations(r) ignores order, permutations(r) respects it

chapters.title: Context Managers and with
points: with obj: calls obj.__enter__(), binds its return value via as, and always calls obj.__exit__(exc_type, exc, tb) on exit
__exit__ returning a truthy value suppresses the exception; returning None or False lets it propagate
@contextlib.contextmanager turns a generator with one yield into a context manager; wrap yield in try/finally so cleanup runs on errors
Without try/finally around yield, an exception in the with body skips the cleanup code in a @contextmanager
contextlib.suppress(Err), closing(obj) and ExitStack (dynamic number of managers) cover the everyday helpers; with a, b: enters managers left to right and exits them in reverse

chapters.title: Cheat Sheet: Iterators, Generators, itertools, with
points: Protocol: iter(x) gives an iterator, next(it) advances, StopIteration signals the end
Generator function (yield) vs generator expression (...) vs list comprehension [...]: lazy and one-shot vs eager and reusable
itertools one-liners: islice(count(), 5), chain(a, b), groupby(sorted(d, key=k), key=k), product(a, b)
Context manager skeleton: @contextmanager def cm(): res = setup(); try: yield res; finally: cleanup
Top gotchas: exhausted generators are empty, groupby needs sorted input, bare yield without try/finally leaks cleanup
